atom.evidence_excerpt:
Criteria for BPD:
1 Intense and unstable relationships, alternating between extremes of idealization 
and devaluation: quickly enters into new romantic relationships, idealizes the 
other person, and allows him/herself to be seduced or infatuated, which reduces 
his/her social judgment; does the opposite when disappointment arrives, seeing 
only the negative in the person where before they could see only the positive.
2 Has difficulties with being alone and strong feelings associated with being 
abandoned: therefore, he/she makes desperate efforts to avoid being aban-
doned, for example, allowing him/herself to be treated poorly, acting sub-
missively, carrying out dramatic acts such as injuring him/herself, or 
threatening to commit suicide
3 Identity problems: fluctuating self-esteem, unstable self-image, constant 
changes in life goals, difficulties in holding on to one’s inner core self
4 Impulsivity that can be self-destructive (i.e., impulsive risk-taking): for exam-
ple, purchasing things one can’t afford, driving recklessly and/or above the 
speed limit, acting on poorly considered decisions, promiscuity, abuse/mis-
use of alcohol and drugs, etc.
5 Self-destructive acts: such as self-mutilation and suicide attempts (to regulate 
painful emotional states)
6 Recurrent feelings of inner emptiness and meaninglessness
7 Constant mood swings: for example, fluctuating between intense dysphoria 
and euphoria in a single day, or between happiness and sadness, bitterness or 
anger
8 Intense anger that is difficult to control (e.g., that may result in throwing 
things, swearing or physical fighting)
9 Reacting with suspiciousness or a feeling of being outside of oneself when stressed.
atom.extraction_notes: 该原子直接提取了BPD的九项标准，并指出这些特质在MBT项目中常见。

atoms.claim: 改善心智化使个体情绪上更坚韧，对人际冲突的脆弱性降低，能更好地处理冲突，且更少冲动。

atoms.claim: 为从心智化治疗中获得最大收益，需要尽可能搁置不信任，对自己保持好奇，并接受临床医生不会评判自己。

atoms.claim: 如果团体中有两位临床医生，他们互相交谈，阐述或质疑对方的话，甚至挑战对方，这模拟了心智化的互动过程，并表明分歧可以是迈向更好理解的积极一步。

atom.claim: MBT小组每次75分钟，这是与患者和临床医生广泛协商后确定的，因为90分钟对于注意力控制和情绪刺激管理来说太长。
therapeutic_implications: 75分钟时长足以围绕人际问题产生心智化过程，并有时间挑战过度使用回避型人际策略，但足够短以防止情绪状态过度刺激。
atom.evidence_excerpt: MBT groups are held weekly and each session lasts 75 minutes (Box 12.8). This length of time was chosen after extensive consultation with patients and clinicians; both groups concluded that 90 minutes was too long to concentrate, to work effectively given problems with attentional control in BPD patients (and perhaps in the clinicians too!), and to manage the level of emotional stimulation safely. A time of 75 minutes was agreed as optimal—long enough to allow the generation of mentalizing process around interpersonal problems and to give time to challenge excessive use of avoidant interpersonal strategies, but short enough to prevent overstimulation of emotional states.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确规定了小组时长及其理由。

atom.claim: MBT-G组织为慢速开放小组，部分出于临床效率，部分为了利用患者离开和新患者加入时所需的心智化过程。
therapeutic_implications: 老患者传递小组历史并引导新患者进入过程，有助于维持小组文化。
atom.evidence_excerpt: MBT-G is organized as a slow open group, partly in the interests of clinical efficiency but also to harness the mentalizing processes that are necessary when a patient leaves and a new patient arrives. The process of engaging a new patient in the group is discussed later in this chapter. The culture of the group is maintained over time by “older” patients passing on the history of the group and inducting new patients into the process.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了慢速开放小组的结构和目的。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 两名临床医生的适应症
atom.claim: 如果患者群体在共病方面严重且患者频繁出现自毁行为，则可能需要两名临床医生。
therapeutic_implications: 两名临床医生可以示范心智化过程，一人管理焦虑或痛苦的患者，另一人继续团体焦点，并减少因假期或生病取消团体的可能性。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 两名临床医生的潜在缺点
atom.claim: 两名临床医生的存在可能让团体成员感到压倒性，并存在一名临床医生与患者结盟对抗另一名临床医生的风险。
therapeutic_implications: 需注意避免团体成员感到被压倒，以及防止临床医生与患者之间的联盟。
atom.evidence_excerpt: the presence of two clinicians can feel overpowering to the group members who already have an individual clinician as well; there is also a risk of alliances developing between one clinician and patient(s) against the other clinician, and so on.
atom.extraction_notes: 原文明确陈述这些缺点。

atoms.claim: 通常建议患者不要在小组外相互接触，除非是治疗计划的一部分（例如社区治疗项目中的同伴支持）。
therapeutic_implications: 限制小组外社交以避免负面影响，但需考虑个体差异
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As a rule, all recommend that patients do not contact each other outside the group unless it is part of a treatment plan, for example, peer support in a community-based therapeutic program.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述关于小组外社交的一般建议。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 小组外社交的潜在影响
atoms.claim: 小组外社交可能对某些个体有积极影响，但也可能让其他小组成员感到被排斥、被背后议论、怨恨，甚至要求临床医生制止。
clinical_signals: 其他成员感到被排斥或怨恨
therapeutic_implications: 需平衡个体获益与小组整体动力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The effects may be positive for some individuals but less so for other group members, who can feel excluded, talked about behind their backs, resentful, and may even demand that the clinician puts a stop to it.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述小组外社交的双重影响。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 小组前和小组后的社交
atoms.claim: 小组前见面和小组后聊天通常被容忍和忽略，但小组之间的接触更有问题。
therapeutic_implications: 区分不同时间点的小组外社交，管理重点在于小组之间的接触
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Meeting up beforehand and chatting afterwards is usually tolerated and ignored. It is the between-group contact that is more problematic.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接区分小组前/后社交与小组间社交的不同处理。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生在管理小组时承担一定程度的权威，但这不应被解释为变得专横。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需在权威与灵活性之间保持平衡
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It has already been mentioned that in MBT-G the clinician takes a level of authority in managing the group. This should not be interpreted as becoming

atom.claim: MBT-G最舒适的规模是六到九名患者，这允许复杂的人际互动而不会使参与者过度刺激。

atom.claim: 所有小组都需要同意参与和投入的原则，包括定期出席、承诺总体目标、出席时头脑清醒（不受药物或酒精影响）、关注彼此的问题、分享、体谅他人以及管理自己的行为。
therapeutic_implications: 明确小组规则有助于维持治疗框架
atom.evidence_excerpt: Any group needs to agree principles of involvement and engagement. Manifestly all have to agree to attend regularly, to commit to the overall aims, to have a clear mind when attending (and thus not to be under the influence of drugs or alcohol), to focus on the problems of each other, to share, to be considerate of others, and to manage their behavior in the group.
atom.extraction_notes: 直接列举小组限制的具体内容。

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，小组外活动应作为需要额外讨论的“问题”来处理，包括治疗师公开表达自己的观点。

therapeutic_implications: 将小组外活动视为需要讨论的问题，而非直接禁止
response_constraints: 避免威权式回应，如直接禁止或威胁终止治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Contact between groups is taken to be a “problem” that needs additional discussion, which includes the clinician presenting his/her views openly.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将小组外接触视为需要讨论的问题，并包含治疗师公开观点。

atoms.claim: 每次小组会议以对上次会议的简要总结开始，由治疗师进行，但鼓励患者补充。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助缺席者跟上主题，并作为所有人的提醒
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We start with a brief summary of the previous group. This allows anyone who was unable to attend the previous session to catch up with the main themes and it acts as a reminder for all of us. One of us [the clinicians] will do the summary, but it is often helpful if any of you have something to add.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文是治疗师对新小组的引言，明确描述了总结环节。

atoms.claim: 随着时间的推移，小组结构成为小组文化的一部分，新加入的成员可以快速了解模式。

atoms.evidence_excerpt: Over time, the structure becomes part of the culture of the group and new members who join the group can be quickly introduced to the pattern.

atom.claim: 对小组外活动采取威权式回应（如声明这是边界违规、应立即停止、否则可能被开除）会破坏小组的整体目的，因为围绕“问题”没有进行心智化工作。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 新成员加入时重申团体目标

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体作为心智化训练场

therapeutic_implications: 通过协商目标促进心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Working on agreement is in itself likely to facilitate the primary aim of the group to act as a training ground for mentalizing.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 团体初始阶段概述心智化过程

atoms.claim: 在团体开始时，临床医生概述心智化过程，强调心智化的互惠性、相互学习、依恋缓解焦虑以及安全探索个人问题的背景。
therapeutic_implications: 建立团体心智化框架
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At the beginning of the group, the clinicians outline the mentalizing process and emphasize the reciprocity of mentalizing, how we learn from each other, and how attachments can allay anxieties and are a context to explore personal concerns safely.

atoms.evidence_excerpt: The purpose of the group is for studying these processes between people, as well as focusing on problem areas that are very common in BPD and/or ASPD.

therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应指出并探索患者是否真正改变想法，还是为了息事宁人而同意

atom.canonical_name_zh: 探索患者是否真正改变想法
atom.canonical_name_en: exploring whether the patient truly changed their mind
atom.claim: 当患者轻易同意他人时，治疗师应探索患者是否真正改变了想法，还是为了息事宁人而同意。
therapeutic_implications: 询问患者是否真正改变想法，还是为了息事宁人
atom.evidence_excerpt: Was she really changing her mind, or simply agreeing with Leslie “for a quiet life,” worrying about upsetting him?
atom.extraction_notes: 文本直接提出这个问题。

atoms.claim: 三角化是在两人对话中插入第三人，创造空间、替代维度和视角。
clinical_signals: 两人对话陷入僵局或需要新视角
therapeutic_implications: 通过引入第三方观察者来丰富理解
atoms.evidence_excerpt: triangulation is creating a space, an alternative dimension and perspective, in the dialogue between two people by inserting a third person.

atoms.claim: 在心智化关系中，主动探索临床医生的贡献。
clinical_signals: 临床医生意识到可能强加观点，合作丧失
therapeutic_implications: 先验证患者被强迫谈论的感受，然后澄清临床医生的贡献，探索患者屈服的倾向
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In mentalizing the relationship, the contribution from the clinician is actively explored.

atom.claim: 三角化包括：识别重要互动、注意观察者、分离主角、主动探索观察者的体验或想法。
therapeutic_implications: 系统性地引入第三方视角
atom.evidence_excerpt: Clinician identifies important interaction between participants; Notes the observer(s); Separates the protagonists; Actively explores the observer(s)’ own experience of the interaction (talk about self) or about his/her/their thoughts about the observed interaction (talk about others).

atom.claim: MBT的安全原则要求临床医生确保不接管患者的心智化，不强加自己的理解。
clinical_signals: 临床医生可能强加自己的观点
therapeutic_implications: 避免破坏安全原则
response_constraints: 临床医生不应接管患者的心智化或强加理解
atom.evidence_excerpt: This breaks the safety principle in MBT of the clinician ensuring he/she does not take over the mentalizing of the patient and force his/her understanding on the patient.

atoms.claim: 在两名患者进行亲密对话时，过早让其他人介入可能具有破坏性；过晚则可能失去增加详细视角和理解的机会。
clinical_signals: 两名患者正在进行亲密对话
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生需凭敏感性决定何时让其他患者参与对话
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Involving others in an intimate conversation between two group members too early can be disruptive; too late and the potential for increasingly detailed perspectives and understanding is lost because the minds of the other patients are no longer attending to the issue under scrutiny.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明三角化时机的考虑

atoms.claim: 在严重人格障碍患者中，配对更常导致其他成员坐着观看并逐渐游离，而非形成有益的组织性想法。
clinical_signals: 两名患者形成共谋的同一性和同意
其他成员坐着观看并逐渐游离
therapeutic_implications: MBT-G避免对小组过程本身进行解释，而是通过三角化干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: However, in patients with severe personality disorder the converse is more common; they tend to sit and watch and slowly drift away.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述严重人格障碍患者中配对的结果

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生配对时的三角化
atoms.claim: 当两名临床医生与一名患者互动时，他们被视为一个人，互动在心理上是二元的，同样会干扰小组的整体心智化。
clinical_signals: 两名临床医生都专注于一名患者
临床医生可能长时间未意识到小组其他成员
therapeutic_implications: 在MBT-G中，临床医生有明确协议：如果一人专注于患者，另一人应考虑三角化并干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Of particular significance is ensuring that triangulation takes place when two clinicians become involved with one patient. In this context, the clinicians are viewed as one person; that is, the interaction is psychologically dyadic even though there are three people involved.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生配对时需三角化

atom.claim: 三角化是一种干预措施，用于处理自我-他人互动崩溃或即将崩溃为自我-自我互动的情况。
clinical_signals: 两个患者之间或临床医生与患者之间的互动变得对小组其他成员不可及
互动隔离表明心智化已开始从自我-他人转向自我-自我
therapeutic_implications: 通过主动将“他人”心智化插入对话中，防止崩溃为非心智化过程
atom.evidence_excerpt: Triangulation is an intervention addressing the collapse or imminent collapse of self–other interaction into self–self interaction.
atom.extraction_notes: 直接定义三角化干预

atoms.claim: 在MBT-G中，临床医生将对话三角化至特定个体，而非整个团体。
therapeutic_implications: 指定个体迫使互动过程，防止团体陷入无效沉默
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-G, the clinician triangulates to a specific person. Rarely does he/she triangulate to the group as a whole by saying, for example, “What do others think?” “Has anyone else any thoughts about this?” Specifying an individual forces the interactive process and does not allow the group to easily sink into ineffectual silence.

atoms.claim: 边缘型人格障碍患者常难以抑制主导欲望以关注次主导过程，因此可能需要使用停车技术。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者暂时搁置自身强烈愿望，以便关注他人相关话题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Problems with attentional control are frequent in patients with BPD and other personality disorders. Patients often find it hard to suppress a dominant desire in order to attend to a subdominant process. This means they may not be able to easily focus on a topic of relevance and importance to another person if they, themselves, have a strong desire to talk about something affecting them.

validation_errors.error: evidence_excerpt is not verbatim in source chunk

atom.canonical_name_zh: 三角化聚焦：关于他人或关于自我
atom.canonical_name_en: triangulation focus: about them or about me in response to them
atom.claim: 三角化干预可聚焦于被引入患者对其他主角心智状态的看法，或聚焦于其自身在观察对话时的状态和反应。
therapeutic_implications: 两种焦点可交替使用，以监测对互动性心智化的影响
atom.evidence_excerpt: The slight difference in emphasis between these two aspects of triangulation is whether the intervention focuses the patient who is brought in through triangulation on the mind states of the other protagonists or on his/her own state of mind and reactions formed by observing and listening to the dyadic dialogue— “about them” or “about me in response to them.”

atoms.claim: MBT临床医生持续监控所有患者的唤醒水平，遵循唤醒必须维持在中等范围的原则，以促进而非阻碍心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 维持唤醒在中等范围以促进心智化
response_constraints: 临床医生需持续警惕行为或心理的唤醒指标
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT clinicians constantly monitor the arousal levels of all patients, following the MBT principle that arousal has to be maintained within a moderate range, neither too high nor too low, if mentalizing is to be facilitated rather than impeded.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了监控唤醒水平的原则和目的。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 识别患者体验而非问题内容
atoms.canonical_name_en: identifying the experience of the patient rather than the content of the problem
atoms.claim: 在停车技术中，临床医生识别患者的体验而非问题内容。
clinical_signals: 患者无法维持注意力控制
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者聚焦于次主导主题
response_constraints: 临床医生需主动帮助患者聚焦
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Identifies the experience of the patient rather than the content of the problem
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表，明确陈述。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 主动帮助患者聚焦次主导主题
atoms.canonical_name_en: actively helps the patient focus on a subdominant theme
atoms.claim: 临床医生主动帮助患者聚焦于次主导主题。
clinical_signals: 患者无法维持注意力控制
therapeutic_implications: 提高注意力控制
response_constraints: 临床医生需主动帮助
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Actively helps the patient focus on a subdominant theme
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_en: keeping a lid on the dominant desire
atoms.claim: 临床医生通过暂时释放压力来抑制患者的主导欲望。
clinical_signals: 患者有主导欲望需要表达
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者维持注意力控制
response_constraints: 临床医生需暂时让患者释放压力
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Keeps a lid on the dominant desire by momentarily letting off steam
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 临床医生不能忘记已停车患者
atoms.canonical_name_en: clinician must not forget he/she has parked a patient
atoms.claim: 临床医生不能忘记已“停车”的患者，如果患者变得过度焦虑，可能需要暂停小组。
therapeutic_implications: 确保患者被关注，避免遗忘
response_constraints: 临床医生需记住已停车患者
必要时暂停小组
atoms.evidence_excerpt: ◆ Clinician must not forget he/she has “parked” a patient—may have to pause the group if the patient becomes excessively anxious.
atoms.extraction_notes: 来自Box 12.19的要点列表。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 以稍微秘密的方式请求患者等待
atoms.canonical_name_en: slightly conspiratorially asking the patient to wait
atoms.claim: 临床医生以稍微秘密的方式请求患者等待，这会让患者感到特别和被关注。
therapeutic_implications: 让患者感到特别和被关注
response_constraints: 临床医生需以稍微秘密的方式请求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Often, this is best done slightly conspiratorially as this will make the patient feel special and attended to by the clinician.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了以秘密方式请求等待的效果。

atoms.canonical_name_en: openly asking the patient to wait
atoms.claim: 临床医生也可以公开请求患者等待，例如说“Rachel，你能稍等一下吗？我们和Peter先结束，马上回来找你。”
therapeutic_implications: 让患者感到被看见
response_constraints: 临床医生需公开请求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: But, equally, it can be stated openly—“Rachel, can you hang on a short time so that we can finish off this with Peter. We will be back to you in a minute.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了公开请求等待的方式。

atom.claim: 临床医生通过“停车”患者来帮助其生成注意力控制能力，并借助积极治疗联盟促进这一过程。
clinical_signals: 患者无法维持注意力控制
患者表现出激动（如抖脚、过度移动、试图打断）或退缩（如低头、偷看、显得心事重重）
therapeutic_implications: 帮助患者提高注意力控制能力
改善人际关系中的对话来回
response_constraints: 临床医生需以稍微秘密或公开的方式请求患者等待
确保患者感到被当作一个人看待
atom.evidence_excerpt: The aim of the clinician “parking” a patient is to help them generate this capacity, facilitated by the use of a positive therapeutic alliance.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了停车技术的目的和辅助因素。

atoms.claim: 停车技术是治疗师在团体中行使权威的一种方式，确保患者的唤醒水平和需求得到识别和管理。
clinical_signals: 无法集中注意力于当前讨论
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师通过承认患者的需求并请求其等待，帮助患者暂时抑制谈论自己问题的冲动
治疗师需要知道患者能被‘停车’多久
必要时需明确‘取消停车’并‘停车’当前活跃的患者
response_constraints: 治疗师需记住谁被‘停车’了，并适时敏感地回到他们的关注点
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It will be apparent that parking is a further way in which the clinician takes some authority in the group. He/she ensures that arousal levels and patient imperatives are recognized and managed.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述停车是治疗师行使权威的方式，确保识别和管理唤醒水平和患者需求。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 停车技术作为明示线索
atoms.claim: 停车作为一种明示线索，使患者感到被承认为一个‘主体’，一个有需求的人。
therapeutic_implications: 明示线索向患者发出信号，表明治疗师有沟通意图针对其需求，但要求其等待
鼓励患者管理内部压力，不主导话语或对他人提出要求
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Parking serves as an ostensive cue making the patient feel recognized as an “agent,” a person who has needs. This ostensive cue signals to the patient that the clinician has a communicative intention addressed to his/her needs but asks that he/she waits for a short time while other concerns are dealt with.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接陈述停车作为明示线索，使患者感到被承认为主体，并传达治疗师的沟通意图。

atom.claim: 治疗师可能需要在团体互动中主动站在患者一边，这被称为‘站边’。
therapeutic_implications: 站边不仅仅是支持患者，还需要治疗师充当心智
atom.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes the clinician may have to actively take the side of a patient during an interaction in the group. This is known as “siding.” This is more than simply being supportive to a patient, and requires the clinician to act as the mind
atom.extraction_notes: 直接定义站边，并指出其超出简单支持，需要治疗师充当心智（句子未完整，但已提取可用部分）。

atoms.canonical_name_en: maintaining reasonable levels of attachment arousal
atoms.claim: 支持弱势患者的目的是维持适度的依恋唤醒水平并降低即时压力。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生通过支持弱势患者来降低即时压力
临床医生确保其他患者不会变得脆弱或感到受攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The aim is to maintain reasonable levels of attachment arousal and to reduce the immediate stress of the situation
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了支持弱势患者的目标。

atoms.claim: 当脆弱患者状态更稳定时，临床医生必要时可以转换支持对象。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生在脆弱患者稳定后可能转换支持对象
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Clinician switches sides if necessary when the vulnerable patient is more stable.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了转换支持对象的条件。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 另一位临床医生扮演对抗者角色
atoms.canonical_name_en: other clinician takes the position of antagonist
atoms.claim: 当一位临床医生支持弱势患者时，另一位临床医生（如果在场）可以扮演对抗者的角色。
clinical_signals: 一位临床医生正在支持弱势患者
therapeutic_implications: 另一位临床医生采取对抗者立场
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Other clinician (if present) takes the position of antagonist
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了另一位临床医生的角色。

atom.claim: 当一名患者在群体互动中变得日益脆弱时，临床医生应主动站在该患者一边。
clinical_signals: 患者与其他患者或群体之间的对话中患者脆弱性增加
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生迅速评估最脆弱患者的心智状态
临床医生代表患者发言，例如说“那有点苛刻，Karen。你能试着用不同的方式表达你的意思吗？”
临床医生在必要时继续代表脆弱患者行事
确保其他患者不会变得脆弱或感到受攻击
response_constraints: 临床医生代表患者发言
临床医生持续支持脆弱患者直到其心智化重新点燃
atom.evidence_excerpt: The key indicator for the clinician to start taking sides is if one patient is becoming increasingly vulnerable in the context of a discourse either between him/her and another patient or between the patient and the rest of the group.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了临床医生开始支持弱势患者的指征。

atoms.claim: 当一名成员被另一名成员攻击时，临床医生可以站在被攻击者一边，将焦点转回攻击者，以减轻被攻击者的压力。
clinical_signals: 一名成员被另一名成员批评或贬低
therapeutic_implications: 暂时支持被攻击者可以降低其应激水平
response_constraints: 之后需要监控攻击者的反应，因为攻击者也可能变得脆弱
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At this point the clinician has taken the side of Andrea and pushed the focus back to Catherine. This will reduce Andrea’s stress. Now the clinician has to monitor the effect on Catherine as she, too, may become vulnerable.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了临床医生站在Andrea一边并转移焦点，以及需要监控Catherine的反应。

atoms.claim: 当临床医生将焦点保持在攻击者身上时，需要确保在一定程度上支持该成员。
clinical_signals: 攻击者感到被忽视或不被喜欢
therapeutic_implications: 在挑战攻击者的同时提供支持，有助于维持治疗联盟
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The clinician is keeping the focus on Catherine at this point but trying to ensure that he supports her to some extent.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生在保持焦点于Catherine的同时试图支持她。

atoms.claim: 当紧张降低后，临床医生可以不再偏袒任何一方，将焦点重新转回最初被攻击的成员。
therapeutic_implications: 促进被攻击者反思自己的体验
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The conversation continued, and as the tension reduced the clinician passed the focus back to Andrea, no longer taking sides.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述紧张降低后临床医生将焦点转回Andrea且不再偏袒。

atoms.claim: 临床医生可以要求成员在感到挫败时直接说出来，而不是通过批评表达。
clinical_signals: 成员对另一成员感到挫败
therapeutic_implications: 促进直接沟通，减少间接攻击
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the group members were tasked by the clinician to make sure that if they were becoming frustrated when talking to Andrea they should say so.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明临床医生要求成员说出挫败感。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 要求成员监控自身行为
atoms.claim: 临床医生可以要求被攻击的成员监控自己的消极行为，并识别有帮助的互动。
clinical_signals: 成员表现出持续的消极态度

atom.evidence_excerpt: Breaks in treatment are particularly difficult times for people with ASPD and may be associated with an increased risk of “acting out.” ... It is important not to collude with the participants’ conscious rejection of their need for treatment, and be alert to them becoming more disturbed during breaks in treatment, which they may find difficult to acknowledge. ... Similarly, difficult feelings regarding the ending of therapy should be anticipated and discussed if possible, to avert premature dropout.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确针对ASPD人群，强调治疗中断的风险和管理策略。

atom.evidence_excerpt: If one participant leaves the group in the context of an altercation with another group member, one of the clinicians (if two are running the group) may go out to talk to the participant while the remaining clinician works to calm down the situation in the group. atom.claim: 针对最严重和持久的精神障碍（精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）患者家属的心理教育有坚实的证据基础，能减少家庭互动的负面影响并降低患者住院率。
therapeutic_implications: 减少家庭互动的负面影响
降低患者住院率
population: families of patients with schizophrenia and bipolar affective disorder
atom.evidence_excerpt: Psychoeducation delivered by mental health professionals for families of patients with the most severe and enduring mental disorders (schizophrenia and bipolar affective disorder) is routinely provided and is grounded in a robust evidence base (Leff, Kuipers, Berkowitz, Eberlein-Vries, & Sturgeon, 1982; Leff & Vaughn, 1985). Intervention reduces the negative effects of family interactions and, by doing so, reduces patient hospitalizations.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确陈述了心理教育对精神分裂症和双相情感障碍患者家属的证据基础及效果。

atom.claim: 每次会议遵循特定格式：开场（首次为个人介绍，其他为上周反馈）、总结上周并报告技术实践、提问、概述当前主题、交付相关材料并练习、总结、结束并建议家庭练习。

atom.evidence_excerpt: Each session follows a particular format. At the opening of each session (except for the first session, which opens with the personal introductions), family members briefly say how the past week has been and outline any important events that have taken place with their relative with BPD. ... Presenters then summarize what was covered in the previous session. ... Presenters then summarize what they will cover in the current session, and why the content is relevant to family members of people with BPD (see Box 14.3).

atoms.evidence_excerpt: Thus, it is not for the supervisor to tell the supervisee what it was in the patient’s discourse that “they had missed”: that would entail the supervisor taking a nonmentalizing stance.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 督导者从被督导者视角出发

atoms.evidence_excerpt: The task of the supervisor is to take the perspective of the supervisee as his/her starting point, to validate that perspective before offering an alternative, in just the same way as the clinician starts the recovery of mentalizing by validating the patient’s understanding.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 督导中回放心智化丧失时刻

atoms.evidence_excerpt: The supervisor listens for loss of mentalizing on the part of the clinician, stops the account at that point, and “rewinds” to the moments before mentalizing was lost.

atoms.canonical_name_en: Avoiding speculation about causes in supervision
atoms.claim: 在监督中，很少努力推测心智化丧失的“原因”或患者产生非心智化话语的动机，这些策略不被认为有帮助。

None of these strategies are considered helpful in dealing with the next occasion when this might happen.

atom.evidence_excerpt: In a cluster-randomized control trial involving 1345 children across nine elementary schools in a city in the United States (Fonagy et al., 2009), the CAPSLE program was found to substantially reduce aggression and improve classroom behavior. The program’s effectiveness was indicated by a reduction in the number of children nominated by their peers as being aggressive, victimized, or engaging in aggressive bystanding. This was confirmed by the observation of reduced disruptive and off-task classroom behavior in schools implementing CAPSLE.

atom.claim: 照顾者必须显示出自身的情感表现并非真实的状态，这种镜映的特征称为标记性。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 由于情感镜映是表征架构的发展基础，照顾者必须显示出自身的情感表现并非真实的状态：也就是说，父母镜映出的情感并不是父母自身的真实感受。我们将这种镜映的特征称为「标记性」。

atoms.claim: 父母的情感镜映是一种工具，能帮婴儿创建出对自身原初情感状态的正确次级表征，以增强婴儿情感调节的能力。

atoms.claim: 投射性认同是边缘型人格障碍症患者惯用的防卫机制，通过外化异化自我来满足自我统合感的需求。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 我们相信这种历程就是临床上所见的「投射性认同」(projective identification)，也就是边缘型人格障碍症(borderline personality disorder，BPD)患者所惯用的防卫机制。

atoms.claim: 当个体无法用心智化能力处理创伤中的强烈羞愧感，且自身感受与客观现实之间几乎没有距离时，会经验到自我好像要被摧毁，称为自我毁灭性的羞愧。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 由于自身感受与客观现实之间几乎没有距离，所以这种无法心智化的羞愧感出现时，个体就会经验到自我好像要被摧毁了一样，我们将其称为「自我毁灭性的羞愧」（ego-destructive shame）。

atom.claim: 在精神等同模式下，个体感觉内在等同于外在，存于心智中的事物必然也存在于外界，反之亦然。

atom.claim: 如果父母在照顾婴儿时极度不敏感，也无法与婴儿保持同调，婴儿会被迫内化客体（母亲）的心智表征来成为自我的核心，形成异化自我。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 如果父母在照顾婴儿时极度不敏感，也无法与婴儿保持同调，那么心理自我的建构将会出现问题。我们跟随着温尼考特(Winnicott 1967)所说的，如果婴儿无法在母亲的心智中找到他自己，那么他就只能找到母亲。婴儿会被迫内化客体(母亲)的心智表征来成为自我的核心。但在这样的状况中，内化进来的东西是「异化」的，因此无法与本体的自我结构相连在一起。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 反思功能与内省的区分
atom.canonical_name_en: distinction between reflective function and introspection
atom.claim: 反思功能与内省不可混为一谈；内省仅能用意识或自陈方式理解心智状态，而反思功能是潜意识中阐释人类行为的自动化历程。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 读者必须注意，反思功能与内省(introspection)绝不可混为一谈。博尔顿与希尔(Bolton & Hill 1996)指出，内省的缺点在于，它仅能用意识或是自陈的方式来理解心智状态，而不是一种真的能体会心智状态的能力，所以内省无法协助个体调整行为。内省或自我反省(self-reflective)，与反思功能有很大的差异，后者指的是一种在潜意识中阐释人类行为的自动化历程。
atom.extraction_notes: 明确区分反思功能与内省，指出内省是意识自陈，反思功能是潜意识自动化。

atom.evidence_excerpt: 有些人可能会说，反思功能的这个概念与梅兰妮•克莱恩所提的忧郁心理位置最为相近，因为忧郁心理位置的概念就是：一个人开始能够了解他人的伤痛，并且知道自己在那个过程中所参与的部分。反思能力也很类似比昂(Wilfred Bion)(1962a，1962b)所描述的「阿尔法功能」(αfunction)。...温尼考特(1962)曾提过，照顾者若能对婴儿有心理上的理解，就能让婴儿产生出「真我」(true self)。
atom.extraction_notes: 明确将反思功能与克莱恩、比昂、温尼考特的概念关联。

atoms.claim: 成功的涵容能力所带来的结果是安全依附，不安全依附可视为婴儿对照顾者防卫行为的认同，牺牲反思功能来换取亲近。

atoms.claim: 基本情绪由九种型态定义：普遍讯号的不同、在其他灵长类面前呈现的不同状态、生理学上的不同、因普遍的前置事件而不同、多种情绪信号的统合、突然发生的、短暂的、自动化评估的、自动产生的。

atoms.claim: 施华德认为情绪是能让身体感受与情感成形并具有意义的复杂叙事结构，不能单以表情理解。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 人类学家施华德(Shweder)以更激进的方式批评基本情绪理论的观点。施华德认为，有些情绪很难用脸部表情表现出来，所以我们不能单单以表情来理解情绪，而应该把情绪当成「能让身体感受与情感成形，并具有意义的复杂叙事结构」。
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用施华德的观点。

atoms.claim: 勒杜克斯认为脑中有两种情绪系统：第一型源自杏仁核，自动、快速、粗糙；第二型与新皮质有关，可运用认知元素，受主观意志操控。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 根据勒杜克斯所言，脑中有两种主要的情绪系统：第一种源自于杏仁核，这套系统的情绪是自动产生并且本质上较为粗糙，因此这套系统被形容为「既快又狠」；而第二套系统则与大脑的新皮质有关，让我们能运用认知元素来回应情绪。
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用勒杜克斯对两种情绪系统的描述。

atoms.claim: 第二型情绪反应非诱发而是发散，因个体而异，反映个体利用过去经验协助当前判断，可受主观意志操控。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 第二类的情绪反应并不是被诱发，而是发散出去。这种反应会因个体而异，不是普世皆同的，它反映出个体会利用过去的经验，以协助当前的情境做出判断的历程。与第一型相反，第二型情绪可以经由我们的主观意志所操控。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 原初自我、核心自我与自传性自我
atom.claim: 达马西奥区分出三种不同的自我感知：原初自我、核心自我与自传性自我。原初自我是脑部装置的集大成，在一定范围内持续且无意识地维持身体状态；核心自我让我们能与当下的经验做连结；自传性自我由延伸意识产生，提供认同与个人感。

atoms.claim: 同理心定义为一种机制，能够让个体接触他人的观点并做出推想，并在某种程度上会经验到对方的情绪状态，这种机制就是IIM-a。

atoms.evidence_excerpt: 华森认为，后效—侦测这个机制当中，有一个重要的功能是自我侦测。个人在做动作时所产生的刺激基本上就是完美的反应后效（例如看着自己正在挥舞的双手），而与外界互动所产生的刺激通常都是较低的反应后效。所以个人的动作与接收到的刺激间后效程度的高低，就变成一开始区分自我与外在世界的标准。

atoms.claim: 后效-侦测机制的一个功能是自我侦测，个人动作产生的刺激是完美的反应后效，与外界互动产生的刺激是较低的反应后效，以此区分自我与外在世界。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 个人在做动作时所产生的刺激基本上就是完美的反应后效（例如看着自己正在挥舞的双手），而与外界互动所产生的刺激通常都是较低的反应后效。所以个人的动作与接收到的刺激间后效程度的高低，就变成一开始区分自我与外在世界的标准。

atom.claim: 后效-侦测机制是生理回馈与情感镜映的基本机制，父母的情感镜映帮助婴儿敏感于自己的情绪状态线索并加以分类。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 后效—侦测机制的其中一个功能，便是掌握个体对于内在状态线索的敏感度，这也是生理回馈训练的目标。……在发展过程中，父母的情感镜映也会帮助婴儿能敏感于自己的情绪状态线索，并将其加以分类。而我们假设这同样也是基于后效—侦测机制的原理。

atoms.claim: 父母的情感镜映对婴儿的情绪状态调节有重要性，通过后效-侦测与后效-最大化的历程帮助婴儿情感调节。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 我们坚称，父母的情感镜映对婴儿的情绪状态调节，就是有这么大的重要性。以下会开始解释后效—侦测与后效—最大化的历程，是如何帮助父母诠释婴儿的情绪，进而帮助婴儿的情感调节。

atoms.claim: 父母的情感表达带有一种特殊的知觉特征称为「标记性」，使婴儿能理解父母反映的是婴儿自身的情感而非父母自己的情感。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 我们认为这个情绪归因问题的答案，是因为父母的情感表达带有一种特殊的知觉特征，我们把它称为「标记性」。

atoms.claim: 中断式安抚与镜映式安抚的差别在于婴儿是否有经验到转化自身情绪的掌控感；中断式安抚中婴儿经验到自己是被动被调节的。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 中断式安抚与镜映式安抚最大的差别在于，婴儿是否有经验到转化自身情绪的掌控感。受到父母镜映式调节的婴儿，会经验到自己是个主动并且有因果效能的主体，对自己的状态调节有种后效控制感，反之，受到中断式调节的婴儿，他的状态变化之因果会与外在的主体或事件有关。

atoms.claim: 婴儿通过后效分析机制体验到因果互效，即自己能够影响父母的情感镜映表现，从而增进正向情感并降低负向情感。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 后效分析机制也会用另一种方式影响婴儿的情感调节，让婴儿更能控制与唤来父母的情感镜映，那就是因果互效(causal efficacy)。

atoms.claim: 父母的情感镜映让婴儿开始建立一种感受：自我是一个能自我调节的主体。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 所以我们能假设，父母的情感镜映不只成功地调节了婴儿的情感，还让婴儿开始建立一种感受：自我是一个能自我调节的主体。

atoms.claim: 当必要系数高于充分系数时，婴儿会降低自身情绪反应的频率与强度，以趋近两个系数，从而获得对父母镜映表现的最大控制感，这便是情绪调节。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 根据后效最大化的假设，当必要系数高于充分系数时，将会使婴儿减少反应的层级，来让两个系数更加趋近，这样他们才能知道自己能够影响父母亲镜映表现的真实程度。而结果就是，婴儿会降低自身情绪反应的频率与强度。在一连串的作用下，为了对父母亲的镜映表现达到最大的控制感，婴儿因而降低了负面情绪表达的频率与强度，这便是情绪调节(消除负向情绪)。

atom.claim: 镜映行为无法长期持续，总是会被打断，这种不断循环的特征可能是因为对另一个主体的同理认同本质就是短暂的。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 镜映行为无法长期持续，总是会被打断，这种不断循环的特征可能是因为对另一个主体的同理认同，本质就是短暂的，而且同理性的情感表达本就倾向于简短的动作或姿势，而不是一种持续性的表达状态。

atoms.claim: 标记性情感镜映是指父母用夸张的方式表达情感，使其与真实情感不同，从而帮助婴儿区分情感归属。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 「标记」基本上指的是将真实的情感用更为夸张的方式来表达⑪ ，与在玩假扮游戏时会出现的那种「好像是真的」(as if)的情感表达很像。

atoms.claim: 参照定向是指婴儿通过后效关系将脱钩的情感定向回自身，从而理解情感反映的是自己的状态。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 婴儿得进行参照定向(referential anchoring)，以找出那到底是谁的情感，这个历程是由于父母的情感反映与婴儿的情绪表达间那高度的后效关系所致。

atoms.claim: 中断式安抚是指父母引入另一种强烈情感来阻断婴儿原有情感，婴儿被动被调节，缺乏后效控制感。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 这种调节方式的意思是，父母会引入另一种强烈的情感来阻断婴儿原先的情感，像是把婴儿「丢高高」或是对他骚痒。这些介入方式对婴儿正在进行的状态一点后效性也没有，所以婴儿可能会经验到自己是「被动」被调节的。

atoms.claim: 标记性情感镜映使婴儿建立次级表征结构，形成对自身情绪状态的前象征次级情绪表征。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: 藉由母亲「标记」过的情感表达，能使一套不同版本的表征介入原来的表征结构，如此一来，婴儿便开始能运用次级的表征结构(secondary representational structure)，往后，每当婴儿的内在状态线索与特定的情绪意向吻合时，婴儿就会自动启动次级的表征结构，在意识上对自己的情绪状态形成一种「前象征」(proto-symbolic)的次级情绪表征，并知道这是他自己的情绪状态。

atoms.claim: 情感镜映是指父母反映婴儿的情感状态，通过标记性表达帮助婴儿调节情绪并发展表征能力。

atom.claim: 情感镜映社会生物回馈理论假定婴儿会直觉性地把情感状态的动态变化用行为表达出来，母亲会用标记性形式回应，具有调节情感和提供鹰架环境的功能。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 我们的情感镜映社会生物回馈理论假定婴儿与照顾者间有复杂的生物社会系统，而婴儿会直觉性地把自己情感状态的动态变化，用行为表达出来。此时母亲也会直觉性地用一种「标记性」的形式，来回应婴儿想要表达自己状态的行为。这样的系统具有两种发展上的主要功能：（a）为婴儿情感状态的变化提供一种在线的调节，使之能维持恒定，与（b）提供某种「教导」或「鹰架」式的环境，让婴儿能够建立原始情感状态的次级表征，从而内化母亲的情感调节功能。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 缺少标记性的异常镜映
atom.claim: 缺少标记性的异常镜映：父母在情感镜映时情绪归类正确但缺乏标记，导致婴儿认定情感是照顾者的真实情绪，无法建立次级表征，并可能发展出投射性认同等病态特征。
atom.evidence_excerpt: 有些父母在情感镜映时，虽然情绪归类是正确的，但却会在知觉上缺乏标记...根据我们的假设，若婴儿长期接收这种异常的镜映型态，就有可能导致以下的结果：（a）由于父母表达的情感镜映缺少标记，这个情感就无法与照顾者自身脱钩，因此婴儿便会认定这个情感就是照顾者的真实情绪；（b）由于情感表现无法与照顾者脱钩，所以也不会定向到婴儿身上，婴儿原初情绪状态的次级表征也就没办法建立...

atom.evidence_excerpt: 以我们的社会生理回馈理论来说的话，比昂谈的这些事情就是：母亲藉由一致并「标记过」的情感回应，来调节婴儿的负向情感而婴儿藉由内摄这种被标记、与真实表现脱钩，且能回应到自己身上的情感回应后，这样的母性经验能让婴儿在自己的原初情绪状态上，建立起次级情绪表征。

atom.claim: 目的论表征基于理性行动原则，即主体在限制性物理环境下会采取最合理或最有效率的方法达成目标。

atom.claim: 在约四至六岁，心理等价与假装模式融合并整合为心智化，但此时心智化是新的且脆弱的，前心智化模式容易重新出现并主导社会认知多年。

atom.evidence_excerpt: At this stage psychic equivalence and pretend mode are fused and welded together and integrated into what we call mentalizing. However, it has to be noted that at this stage, all this is new and vulnerable and the pre-mentalizing modes can easily crop up and dominate social cognition for years (Fonagy & Allison, 2012).

atoms.claim: 在12岁进入青春期时，大脑的“检测节点”已经发育，能够解读和反应各种社会线索，但负责心理化、冲动抑制和目标导向行为的“认知调节节点”尚未成熟。

atoms.evidence_excerpt: In the previous years, what has been developed in the brain is the ‘detection node’, which deciphers and reacts to all sorts of social clues (Nelson, Leibenluft, McClure, & Pine, 2005). The cognitive-regulatory node, responsible for mentalizing, impulse inhibition and goal-directed behaviour, which in other words tells us what to do with all those social circumstances and goings-on, is not as developed.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了青少年大脑发育的差异，属于发展适应内容。

atom.claim: 青少年期社交脑继续发育，包括突触修剪，并且青少年在理解社会世界时使用与成人不同的脑区（更前部区域）。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗中需意识到青少年社会认知的神经基础仍在变化
atom.evidence_excerpt: Other research has also shown that the social brain continues to develop in the adolescent years. This involves developments such as synaptic pruning, namely getting rid of unused neural connections to make the processes more efficient (Choudhury, Charman, & Blakemore, 2008). In addition, adolescents use quite different brain areas when they try to understand the social world; namely the more anterior areas, as opposed to the posterior lateral areas used by adults (Burnett, Bird, Moll, Frith, & Blakemore, 2008; Burnett, Sebastian, Kadosh, & Blakemore, 2011).
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了青少年社交脑的持续发育和脑区差异。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 情绪温度升高导致心智化失衡
atoms.claim: 当互动中紧张情绪过高（情绪温度升高），平衡最终会被打破，人会以非心智化的方式思考和行动。

atoms.evidence_excerpt: When in our interactions tensions get too high (the emotional temperature rises), the balance will eventually be disturbed, sooner or later according to our strengths and weaknesses, and we will react in non-mentalizing ways of thinking and behaving.

atoms.claim: 在目的论模式中，心理状态通过目标导向的行动而非语言等明确的心理表征来表达，例如用自伤来传达极端情绪痛苦。

atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用定义和例子。

atoms.claim: 当主要照顾者因自身问题无法心智化婴儿，而是镜像回自己的恐惧或愤怒时，婴儿会内化他人的恐惧等，形成异己自我。

That would not lead to a sense of recognising oneself but to internalising the fears and so on of the other; in what is called the alien self (Fonagy et al., 2002).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了异己自我的形成机制。

atoms.claim: 如果教养环境未能产生对他人会告知有价值信息的信任，而是让人依赖的人说伤人的、错误的话，那么平衡会转向认识论不信任。

atoms.evidence_excerpt: In summary, the therapist stance requires the following competencies from an MBT therapist (Bateman, Bales, & Hutsebaut, 2012): • An ability to communicate with the patient in a direct, authentic, transparent manner, using simple and unambiguous statements to minimise the risk of over-arousing the client. • An ability to adopt a stance of ‘not knowing’ which communicates to the patient a genuine attempt to find out about their mental experience. • An ability to sustain an active, non-judgmental mentalizing stance that prioritises the joint exploration of the patient’s mental states. • An ability to communicate genuine curiosity about the patient’s mental states through actively enquiring about interpersonal processes and their connection with the patient’s mental states. • An ability to follow shifts and changes in the patient’s understanding of their own and others’ thoughts and feelings. • An ability to become aware of and respond sensitively to sudden and dramatic failures of mentalization in the patient.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，首先验证父亲（家长）的感受，否则他会感到更羞辱而无法心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 先验证感受，再帮助反思
atoms.evidence_excerpt: With this technique, we try and validate the dad’s feeling first; otherwise, he will feel more humiliated and not be able to mentalize.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，可以请父亲像记者一样询问男孩当天的事件，以激发父亲对男孩心智的好奇心。
clinical_signals: 父亲缺乏对儿子心智的好奇
therapeutic_implications: 使用游戏性技巧，如扮演记者
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes it helps to be playful and ask the dad to be an interviewer for a newspaper and to ask the boy about events of the day prior to him kicking the pots.

atoms.claim: 如果男孩不在场，可以请父亲想象从男孩的视角看问题，以理解他的感受和想法。
clinical_signals: 父亲难以理解儿子的行为
therapeutic_implications: 使用想象技巧，如画图加思想气泡
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If the boy is not in the room, one could still get the dad to imagine life from the boy’s perspective to try and understand what he feels and what was going through his mind at the time.

atoms.claim: 当患者因自身心理状态而盲目时，治疗师明确表达自己的感受或意图（如“我不生你的气”）有助于降低患者的唤醒水平。
therapeutic_implications: 明确表达不生气、不评判，站在患者一边
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is very helpful for patients if we explicitly state during these times “I am not angry with you”. Alternatively, when they feel overwhelmed with humiliation or shame, it can be helpful for us to state our feelings explicitly, to avoid them feeling we judge them too, by saying: “I am not angry or judging you, I am on your side. All I want to do, is try and understand”.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 表达自身限制以降低威胁
atoms.canonical_name_en: expressing own limitations to reduce threat
atoms.claim: 治疗师对愤怒的青少年说“当你那样尖叫时，我无法思考”，通过表达自己的限制来降低威胁和青少年的唤醒水平，迫使青少年心智化治疗师。
therapeutic_implications: 表达想听和理解，但指出尖叫让自己无法思考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By communicating that, he stated explicitly his intention of wanting to hear and understand and by saying, “when you scream like that, I cannot think” he presented himself as another human being with his own limitations, therefore reducing the threat and the young person’s arousal levels, and forcing the young person to mentalize him, which kick-started mentalization in the young person.

atom.claim: 在MBT-A中，治疗师要反思与患者的互动，承认自己对患者有情感影响，并为自己误解或错误承担责任。
therapeutic_implications: 承认错误并修复连接
atom.evidence_excerpt: Mentalizing the therapeutic relationship refers to reflecting on the interactions between the therapist and the patient. We take responsibility for the fact that we have an emotional impact on the patient and that we, at times, get things wrong or misunderstand them. When we misunderstand them or get something wrong, we own up to it and try and restore the connection between us.

validation_errors.error: evidence_excerpt is not verbatim in source chunk

atom.claim: 在MBT-A中，治疗师不应解释患者的无意识或提及自己是无意识投射的接收者。
therapeutic_implications: 聚焦此时此地的关系，而非过去的无意识投射
contraindications: 不应做无意识解释
atom.evidence_excerpt: In MBT-A, we do not aim to make interpretations about the patient’s unconscious or make reference to us being the receptors of unconscious projections. The emphasis is on relationships in the here and now, not unconscious projections from the patient’s past.

atoms.claim: 治疗师必须意识到自己犯了错误，并承担责任以修复与患者的连接。
clinical_signals: 患者行为举止突然改变
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应道歉并请求帮助理解错误所在
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We must pick up when we have made an error and then take responsibility for it to try and repair the connection with the patient. If a patient says: “You have not understood me”. We would say: “I am so sorry, I really want to understand you, please help me see where I got it wrong”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师在误解患者后应如何回应。

atoms.claim: 当患者被自己的心理状态蒙蔽时，治疗师明确表达自己的感受或意图是有帮助的。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应明确说“我没有生你的气”或“我没有评判你，我站在你这边”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is sometimes helpful for our patients if we are explicit with what we feel or what our intentions are, mainly when our patients are a bit blinded by their own mental states or, as described earlier, where the shutters are down. For example, if a patient is very angry, either with the therapist or with themselves, they are often likely to think the therapist is angry too. It is very helpful for patients if we explicitly state during these times “I am not angry with you”. Alternatively, when they feel overwhelmed with humiliation or shame, it can be helpful for us to state our feelings explicitly, to avoid them feeling we judge them too, by saying: “I am not angry or judging you, I am on your side. All I want to do, is try and understand”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确说明了在患者情绪强烈时表达治疗师感受的益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 降低唤醒以恢复心智化
atoms.claim: 治疗师承认自己对患者的影响，并尝试重新建立联系以恢复心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应承认自己的影响并重新建立联系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We take full responsibility for the fact that we have an impact upon our patients, and this can sometimes lead to an increase in arousal, and hence compromise the young person’s ability to mentalize. It is important for us to own this and try and re-establish contact with the patient in order to re-instate mentalization.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了治疗师的影响与患者心智化能力的关系。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 通过表达自身局限降低威胁
atoms.canonical_name_en: reducing threat by expressing own limitations
atoms.claim: 治疗师通过表达自己作为人类的局限（如“我无法思考”）来降低威胁和患者的唤醒水平，并促使患者心智化治疗师。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师可以说“我真的很想听和理解你说的话，但如果你这样尖叫，我无法思考”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: By communicating that, he stated explicitly his intention of wanting to hear and understand and by saying, “when you scream like that, I cannot think” he presented himself as another human being with his own limitations, therefore reducing the threat and the young person’s arousal levels, and forcing the young person to mentalize him, which kick-started mentalization in the young person.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了该技术如何降低威胁并启动心智化。

atoms.claim: 在青少年MBT工作中，我们将家庭纳入治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 使家庭成员能够支持和搭建家庭环境的发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: In our work with young people, we involve families in the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 随着家庭更能心智化，家庭成员在某种程度上成为治疗师，在家庭中支持和搭建心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 家庭在家庭中支持和搭建心智化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: as the family becomes more able to mentalize, family members become in a way therapists themselves who can support and scaffold mentalization at home at times when it breaks down.

atoms.claim: MBT-A通常将个体治疗与MBT-家庭和/或MBT-团体相结合。
therapeutic_implications: 在更密集的项目中，个体治疗与家庭和团体治疗结合；在较不密集的项目中，与家庭治疗结合
atoms.evidence_excerpt: MBT-A is a model in which individual therapy is usually combined with MBT-Family and or MBT-Group.

atoms.claim: 家庭治疗不需要每周进行；有初步临床证据表明六次家庭工作可能足够，每两周一次给家庭更多时间应用所学。
therapeutic_implications: 家庭治疗频率可调整为每两周一次
atoms.evidence_excerpt: There is emerging clinical evidence to suggest that six sessions of family work can be sufficient, and stretching it out to twice a month, gives families more time to apply what they have learned.

atoms.claim: 评估过程不应超过三次会谈，且第一次会谈后家庭和青少年通常希望得到反馈或治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估应在三次会谈内完成
第一次会谈后提供反馈或治疗计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our view is that it should not be longer than three sessions and our view is also that after the first session, families and young people usually want some form of feedback or clear idea about the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 如果存在风险问题，需要在第一次会谈中处理，并与青少年和家庭制定危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 第一次会谈中处理风险问题并制定危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there are concerns about risk, this needs to be addressed in the first session too and a crisis plan needs to be developed with the young person and the family.

atoms.claim: 评估阶段通常以讨论个案概念化结束。
therapeutic_implications: 评估阶段结束时讨论个案概念化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The assessment phase is usually concluded with the discussion of the formulation

atom.claim: 在评估过程中，治疗师保持心智化姿态：好奇、开放、不知晓、温暖、共情和真诚。
therapeutic_implications: 评估过程中保持心智化姿态
atom.evidence_excerpt: we do so with a mentalizing mind, which means we are curious, open-minded and we maintain a not-knowing stance with an attitude of warmth, empathy and authenticity.

atoms.claim: 评估阶段通常不超过三次会谈，并在第一次会谈后提供反馈或治疗计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估应高效，避免超过三次会谈
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Our view is that it should not be longer than three sessions and our view is also that after the first session, families and young people usually want some form of feedback or clear idea about the treatment plan.

atoms.claim: 如果存在风险问题，必须在第一次会谈中处理，并与青少年和家庭共同制定危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 首次会谈需包含危机计划制定
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there are concerns about risk, this needs to be addressed in the first session too and a crisis plan needs to be developed with the young person and the family.

atoms.claim: 在MBT-A评估中，临床医生会询问心智化追踪问题，例如“当他那样做时，你觉得他有什么感受？”以了解心智化困难。
therapeutic_implications: 评估中关注心智化困难
atoms.evidence_excerpt: the clinician would pay attention to evidence of good mentalizing or examples of non-mentalizing functioning and hence may ask a few mentalizing tracer questions, such as “when he did that, what do you think he was feeling…”

atoms.claim: 评估结束时，MBT-A临床医生应了解呈现问题与诊断、起草初步个案概念化、描述治疗计划，并在必要时制定清晰的安全或危机计划。
therapeutic_implications: 评估产出包括概念化、治疗计划和危机计划
atoms.evidence_excerpt: At the end of the assessment, the MBT-A clinician would want to be in a position to do the following: • Have an idea of the presenting problems and the diagnosis when this is useful • Draw up a draft formulation of the young person’s difficulties • Describe the treatment plan • Develop a clear safety or crisis plan, when indicated

atoms.claim: 治疗合同是治疗计划的具体描述，明确治疗内容、频率、时长和实际安排，以便青少年和家庭知情同意。
therapeutic_implications: 合同促进知情同意和明确期望
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is more a description of the treatment plan in a concrete way which makes explicit for the young person and family what the treatment will entail, how often the sessions will be, what is being offered and how long it will last. It makes the practical arrangements clear from the start so that the young person and the family know what they can expect, have a clear understanding of what is offered and can sign up for it willingly, or in other words, consent to participate in it.

atoms.claim: 治疗合同中不设定具体期望，如要求青少年停止自伤等行为。
therapeutic_implications: 避免在合同中设定具体行为改变目标
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do not bring in concrete expectations that the young person would stop self-harming or anything along such lines.

atom.claim: 在评估过程中，临床医生应保持好奇、开放、不知晓的态度，并带有温暖、共情和真诚。
therapeutic_implications: 评估时即采用与治疗全程相同的心智化立场
atom.evidence_excerpt: Whenever we meet a new family or young person, we do so with a mentalizing mind, which means we are curious, open-minded and we maintain a not-knowing stance with an attitude of warmth, empathy and authenticity.

atom.claim: MBT-A评估的关键区别在于临床医生与青少年和/或家庭一起心智化，使所有人感到被招募为治疗伙伴，而非临床医生是解决问题的专家。
therapeutic_implications: 评估中建立合作而非专家模式
atom.evidence_excerpt: The main difference between doing an assessment with an MBT-A hat on and any other assessment is that in this assessment, we mentalize with the young person and/or family together in the session. It is important that all leave the assessment feeling recruited to work alongside the clinician as partners in the treatment, rather than the clinician being the expert that will solve the problem or find out who is at fault.

therapeutic_implications: 评估中需注意心智化表现
使用心智化追踪问题
atoms.evidence_excerpt: in the MBT-A assessment, the clinician is also hoping to get an understanding of the mentalizing difficulties experienced by the young person and the family, so the clinician would pay attention to evidence of good mentalizing or examples of non-mentalizing functioning and hence may ask a few mentalizing tracer questions

It makes the practical arrangements clear from the start so that the young person and the family know what they can expect, have a clear understanding of what is offered and can sign up for it willingly, or in other words, consent to participate in it.

atoms.extraction_notes: 明确反对因自伤终止治疗的合同条款。

atoms.claim: 书面概念化对青少年有帮助，他们可以保留并在日后参考，尤其是在感到不知所措时，具体提醒可以支撑他们。
therapeutic_implications: 提供书面概念化
青少年可保留并参考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it can be very helpful for young people to hold onto it and refer back to it at a later stage, especially at times when they may feel overwhelmed and hence unable to remember the session’s discussion without a concrete reminder to scaffold them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了书面概念化对青少年的益处。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 家庭与个体概念化的区分
atoms.canonical_name_en: Distinction between family and individual formulation
atoms.claim: 在MBT-A中，个体治疗师常与青少年讨论其个人概念化，不与其他家庭成员分享；家庭治疗中的概念化则更关注家庭互动而非个人。
therapeutic_implications: 个体概念化不共享给家庭
家庭概念化聚焦互动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As different therapists frequently offer the individual MBT-A work and the MBT family work, the formulation of the young person is often discussed in the young person’s individual therapy and not shared with the rest of the family. In the family sessions, formulations are developed, but those tend to focus more on family interactions and less on one particular individual.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了青少年个体概念化与家庭概念化的区分，属于青少年治疗的适应性安排。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 心智化框架下处理风险行为
atom.canonical_name_en: Addressing risk behaviors in mentalizing framework
atom.claim: 风险行为（如自伤、自杀、暴力、吸毒）需在心智化框架下处理，理解行为背后的感受，表达担忧但承认其可能是管理困难感受的唯一方式，并共同寻找更安全的应对策略。
therapeutic_implications: 心智化风险行为背后的感受
表达担忧
共同寻找安全策略
atom.evidence_excerpt: These issues need to be addressed in a mentalizing framework where we have mentalized the possible feelings underneath the behaviours. We can communicate concern that the risky behaviours can have dangerous consequences or can be undermining of treatment, but that we understand it may have been the only way for some young people to manage difficult feelings until now. We can convey the hope that together, we may be able to find other ways of helping with those feeling states so that they become more understandable and manageable over time. In the meanwhile, particularly in cases of high risk, we can look at some alternative strategies that they can use, which will provide safer ways of coping.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了在心智化框架下处理风险行为的方法。

validation_errors.error: evidence_excerpt is not verbatim in source chunk

atom.claim: 临床医生完成评估后，会形成对青少年和家庭的初步概念化（即心智化他们），然后与青少年（和家庭）讨论并共同完善概念化。
therapeutic_implications: 形成初步概念化
与青少年和家庭共同讨论
atom.evidence_excerpt: As clinicians complete an assessment, they would be in a position to formulate an understanding of the young person and their family... This is what a draft formulation is. When we discuss this with the young person (and the family), we develop the formulation together.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了共同制定概念化的过程。

atoms.claim: 不支持包含‘如果你自伤，治疗将终止’条款的合同。
therapeutic_implications: 应将高风险行为纳入危机计划或合同，而非以终止治疗相威胁
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We do not support contracts that state, ‘if you harm yourself your treatment will be terminated’.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确反对此类合同条款。

atoms.claim: 年轻人转向冲动或自毁行为作为应对方式，如果治疗师不理解这一点并在他们最可能恢复旧有应对方式时撤走治疗，就像在他们跌倒时不帮助其重新站起来。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应理解自伤行为背后的应对功能，而非惩罚或终止治疗
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people turn to impulsive or self-destructive behaviours as a way of coping and if we do not understand that and pull treatment away when they will most likely turn to their old coping styles. It is like leaving someone when they have fallen and not helping them get back on their feet.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确比喻，强调理解和支持的重要性。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 心智化框架下的风险行为处理
atoms.canonical_name_en: addressing risky behaviors within a mentalizing framework
atoms.claim: 风险行为需要在一个心智化框架内处理，其中治疗师心智化了行为背后可能的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 治疗师应表达对危险后果的担忧，同时理解这可能是年轻人管理困难感受的唯一方式，并传达希望共同找到其他帮助方式
atoms.evidence_excerpt: These issues need to be addressed in a mentalizing framework where we have mentalized the possible feelings underneath the behaviours.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确要求在心智化框架下处理。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划中的风险行为讨论
atoms.canonical_name_en: including risky behavior discussions in crisis plan
atoms.claim: 通过心智化视角看待风险行为，将这些讨论纳入危机计划和个案概念化比纳入合同更有意义。
therapeutic_implications: 将风险行为讨论放在危机计划和个案概念化中，而非合同中
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As we see the risky behaviour through a mentalizing lens, it may therefore make more sense to include these discussions in the crisis plan and formulation, rather than in the contract.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确建议纳入危机计划和概念化。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 个案概念化作为心智化过程
atoms.claim: 临床医生完成评估后，能够心智化年轻人及其家庭，以及促使他们寻求专业帮助的问题，这就是草案概念化。
therapeutic_implications: 临床医生应形成对年轻人和家庭的心智化理解，作为概念化草案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: As clinicians complete an assessment, they would be in a position to formulate an understanding of the young person and their family, as well as the issues that brought them to seek professional help. In other words, the clinician would be in a position to mentalize them and see them and the struggle they present with through a mentalizing lens. This is what a draft formulation is.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确将概念化定义为心智化过程。

atoms.claim: 书面概念化对年轻人有帮助，他们可以保留并在以后参考，尤其是在感到不知所措而无法记住讨论内容时。
therapeutic_implications: 提供书面概念化作为具体提醒，帮助年轻人在困难时回顾
atoms.evidence_excerpt: it can be very helpful for young people to hold onto it and refer back to it at a later stage, especially at times when they may feel overwhelmed and hence unable to remember the session’s discussion without a concrete reminder to scaffold them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确书面概念化的支持作用。

atom.claim: 临床医生将草案概念化带给家庭讨论，并共同完善概念化。
therapeutic_implications: 与年轻人和家庭共同讨论和细化概念化
atom.evidence_excerpt: When we discuss this with the young person (and the family), we develop the formulation together. The clinician brings to the family the draft version for discussion and together they elaborate on the formulation.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确共同发展的过程。

atom.claim: 在家庭会谈中，概念化通常侧重于家庭互动，而非某个个体，且通常在会谈中讨论，不以书面形式呈现。
therapeutic_implications: 家庭概念化聚焦互动，口头讨论而非书面
atom.evidence_excerpt: In the family sessions, formulations are developed, but those tend to focus more on family interactions and less on one particular individual. The formulations which develop in family work are usually discussed during the sessions and not presented in written format.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确家庭概念化的特点。

atoms.claim: 个案概念化以类似个人信件的形式呈现给青少年，并作为草稿一起讨论，以确认青少年是否同意，避免被体验为侵入性心智化。
clinical_signals: 青少年可能将治疗师的陈述体验为侵入性心智化
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“是这样吗？”等短语邀请评论，使陈述显得试探性而非事实
atoms.evidence_excerpt: It is presented to the young person as a draft and then discussed together to see if the young person agrees with it. Otherwise, the risk is that it may be experienced as intrusive mentalization, i.e. the therapist telling the young person what they are feeling. Hence, we use phrases in the formulation such as: “is that correct?” Such phrases invite comment from the young person at each stage and read as a tentative statement rather than a fact.

atoms.claim: 在个案概念化中明确表达治疗师的情感（如“看到你对自己如此负面，我感到难过”），将治疗师呈现为有情感的人，帮助青少年更准确地心智化治疗师。
clinical_signals: 青少年以非人化的方式对待自己，并预期治疗师也以同样方式看待他们
therapeutic_implications: 通过明确陈述意图，帮助青少年更准确地心智化治疗师，体现人性
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The reader will also notice comments such as “it makes me feel sad to see how negative you feel about yourself ”. In this way, we explicitly present ourselves as humans with feelings. So often these youngsters relate to themselves in a dehumanising manner and when they do, they anticipate that we view them in the same light. By explicitly stating our intentions, we help them to mentalize us more accurately.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划的心智化方式
atoms.claim: 安全计划应以心智化术语思考风险，处理潜在感受，理解触发因素，并考虑更安全的替代方案。
clinical_signals: 青少年出现自伤、自杀感受或其他风险行为（如暴力）
therapeutic_implications: 与家庭和青少年共同制定安全计划，讨论潜在感受和触发因素，思考更安全的替代方案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The safety plan aims to think about the risk in mentalizing terms and to address the underlying feelings as well as have some understanding of the trigger factors and then to think about safer alternatives that can be used.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年危机计划的数字化适应
atoms.canonical_name_en: digital adaptation of crisis planning for adolescents
atoms.claim: 鉴于青少年生活在网络世界而非纸质世界，作者开发了一款移动应用程序作为危机计划讨论的一部分，但应用程序需要个性化且以心智化方式使用。
clinical_signals: 青少年对纸质危机计划反应不佳
therapeutic_implications: 在讨论危机计划时结合使用移动应用程序，但应用程序必须个性化且以心智化方式使用
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people live in a cyber world and not a paper world anymore. She, therefore, developed a mobile app that she uses as part of the crisis planning discussion with young people. Given that the app is very general, it will not be helpful if crisis planning is exclusively just the app. It needs to be personalised and mentalized in the way that is mentioned above.

atoms.claim: 危机计划应以心智化术语思考风险，处理潜在感受，理解触发因素，并思考更安全的替代方案。
therapeutic_implications: 与家庭和青少年共同制定安全计划
提供书面计划供青少年和家长带回家参考
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The safety plan aims to think about the risk in mentalizing terms and to address the underlying feelings as well as have some understanding of the trigger factors and then to think about safer alternatives that can be used. The safety plan is drawn up with the family and the young person and our view is that it is best if it can be discussed in the session, but also that it can be provided to the young person and their parents in written format so that they can take it home with them and refer to it at a later stage.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了危机计划的目的和制定方式。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 青少年危机计划数字化
atoms.claim: 青少年生活在网络世界而非纸质世界，因此作者开发了一款移动应用程序作为危机计划讨论的一部分。
therapeutic_implications: 在治疗中讨论并演示应用程序
将个性化心智化危机计划与应用程序结合
contraindications: 仅使用通用应用程序而不进行个性化心智化讨论无效
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Young people live in a cyber world and not a paper world anymore. She, therefore, developed a mobile app that she uses as part of the crisis planning discussion with young people. Given that the app is very general, it will not be helpful if crisis planning is exclusively just the app. It needs to be personalised and mentalized in the way that is mentioned above.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划中的延迟与反思
atoms.canonical_name_en: delay and reflection in crisis plan
atoms.claim: 当青少年有冲动行为时，建议尝试延迟行动10分钟，并利用这10分钟反思触发感受的关系事件。
therapeutic_implications: 帮助青少年理解感受和关系触发因素
促进从不同视角思考解决方案
atoms.evidence_excerpt: When you feel like that again, I would like you to try and stop the action by trying to delay it for 10 minutes. Then use the 10 minutes to try and reflect on what was happening a few moments before you had the bad feeling. That might help you to understand more clearly what it is that you feel as well as what might have happened in a close relationship which may have contributed to the feeling.
atoms.extraction_notes: 危机计划示例中的具体步骤。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 为家长提供单独危机计划
atoms.claim: 作者为家长提供单独的危机计划，以指导并帮助他们在家长角色中发挥作用。
therapeutic_implications: 提供家长指导
支持家长角色
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The author also provides a separate crisis plan for parents to guide them and help them in their role as parents.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确提到为家长提供单独计划。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 应对技能应用程序内容
atoms.claim: 应对技能应用程序包含从DBT借用的痛苦耐受技巧、正念练习、心智化练习、引导冥想和渐进式肌肉放松录音，并可链接青少年自己的平静音乐和美好回忆的图片。
therapeutic_implications: 在治疗中与青少年一起浏览应用程序以理解如何使用
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The COPING SKILLS app is a combination of distress tolerance skills, borrowed from DBT, mindfulness exercises, a mentalization exercise and guided meditation as well as progressive muscle relaxation tapes. It also has a functionality where young people can link it to calming music of their own, and also images and photos which hold good memories for them.
atoms.extraction_notes: 详细描述了应用程序内容。

atom.canonical_name_zh: 危机计划中的替代行为
atom.claim: 如果延迟和反思后仍感到自伤风险，建议使用应对技能应用程序中的工具，或通过与人交谈、玩游戏、写诗、绘画、看电视等分散注意力。
therapeutic_implications: 提供具体替代行为
使用应用程序辅助
atom.evidence_excerpt: If that fails and you still feel at risk of harming yourself, use the tools on the COPING SKILLS app to help you. ... Try and bring yourself back to reality – do something to occupy yourself, like talking to someone, playing a game, writing a poem, painting or watching something that can hold your attention on TV.
atom.extraction_notes: 危机计划示例中的具体建议。

atoms.claim: 危机计划包括对青少年自伤和风险的基本理解，以及关于如何应对和说什么/做什么的实用建议。
therapeutic_implications: 为父母提供指导
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The crisis plan with the parents includes some basic understanding of self-harm and risk in young people and practical advice on how to behave and what to say/do when young people self-harm.

atoms.claim: 鼓励关于自伤的沟通，允许青少年在感到有风险时告知父母，例如通过预先约定的表情符号。
therapeutic_implications: 促进青少年表达风险
atoms.evidence_excerpt: encourage communication about self-harm and allow your child to tell you when they feel at risk. Young people will find this very hard to do and for some young people it is easier to agree on an emoji that they can send their parents on their phone as a code that they are at risk of harming themselves.

atoms.canonical_name_en: stay with child at higher risk
atoms.claim: 如果青少年风险较高，父母应陪伴他们，确保他们不独处。
therapeutic_implications: 提供持续监护
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If your child is at higher risk, be with them and ensure that they are not on their own.

atoms.claim: 父母应尝试理解青少年自伤前的感受，并帮助他们谈论感受和事件，即使事件涉及父母，也要倾听并验证其感受，而不必持有相同观点。
therapeutic_implications: 促进情感验证
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Just try and understand what your child felt before they wanted to harm themselves and help them to speak about the feelings and the events leading up to the feelings. If the events involved you, listen and try to understand their perspective without becoming defensive. You don’t have to hold the same perspective, but it is important that you validate their feelings.

atoms.claim: 如果青少年有自杀倾向，父母应明确表示自杀不是选项，表达爱意，并提议转移注意力或寻求帮助。
therapeutic_implications: 提供明确界限和支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If your child is suicidal, you could say: “Killing yourself is not an option. I love you and do not want you to kill yourself. You are not alone. We will get through this together. I am going to stay here with you to keep you safe. Let’s try and think of something that will help right now. Will distraction help such as going for a walk or watching TV?”

atom.claim: 基本安全措施包括锁好药物、将刀具放在够不到的地方、限制使用剃刀以及从青少年卧室移除尖锐物品。
therapeutic_implications: 减少自伤手段的可及性
atom.evidence_excerpt: Keep medication locked away; If your child harms themselves by cutting themselves, it may be helpful if you keep the knives out of reach and restrict access to razors; It may also be helpful if you remove sharps from your child’s bedroom

atom.claim: 当青少年自伤时，父母应倾听、理解并让他们知道你在那里；不要恐慌、责备或惩罚。
therapeutic_implications: 保持非评判性态度
atom.evidence_excerpt: Dos: Listen; Understand; Let them know you are there for them. Don’ts: Panic; Blame; Punish.

atom.claim: 如果青少年非常激动，过多说话无益；应友善和支持，说“我不生你的气，我来帮你并保证你的安全”等话语。
therapeutic_implications: 减少言语刺激，提供安抚
atom.evidence_excerpt: If your child is very aroused, speaking too much is not helpful. Just be kind and supportive and say things like: “I am not angry with you, I am here to help you and keep you safe.”

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应避免的行为
atoms.claim: 父母在危机中不应恐慌、责备或惩罚。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Don’ts: • Panic • Blame • Punish

atoms.evidence_excerpt: Don’t blame your child and don’t blame yourself. Just try and understand what your child felt before they wanted to harm themselves and help them to speak about the feelings and the events leading up to the feelings.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应验证孩子的感受

atoms.claim: 如果父母对误解有贡献，应承认错误，目标是恢复连接而非赢得争论。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If there was a misunderstanding between you which you contributed to, own up to it. You are not here to win battles but to restore the connection between you.

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 危机升级时父母应寻求专业帮助
atoms.claim: 如果所有方法都失败，父母应致电诊所或带孩子去急诊。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: If all else fails, call the clinic or if it is after hours, you may have to take your child to the emergency department.

atom.evidence_excerpt: If your child is very aroused, speaking too much is not helpful. Just be kind and supportive and say things like: “I am not angry with you, I am here to help you and keep you safe.”

atom.canonical_name_zh: 危机中父母应对自伤和自杀的回应
atom.claim: 如果孩子想自伤，父母应表达不希望孩子伤害自己，并提议替代方案如冰敷；如果孩子有自杀倾向，父母应明确表示自杀不是选项，并陪伴孩子寻求安全。
atom.evidence_excerpt: If your child wants to hurt themselves, you could say: “I really don’t want you to hurt yourself. You deserve so much more. Let’s try one of the alternatives. I will help you, shall we get a bowl of ice?” If your child is suicidal, you could say: “Killing yourself is not an option. I love you and do not want you to kill yourself. You are not alone. We will get through this together. I am going to stay here with you to keep you safe.”

atoms.claim: 在无法提供工作坊或心理教育小组的情况下，可以通过在治疗中融入相关陈述来进行非正式心理教育。
therapeutic_implications: 在初始阶段，通过回应治疗材料中的内容，自然地融入心理教育陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Where workshops or psychoeducation groups are not available or possible, psychoeducation can be done more informally, particularly during the initial sessions, by weaving it into the treatment where relevant.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了非正式心理教育的适用情境和方法。

atoms.claim: 心理教育陈述可以用于激发好奇心，并传达心理状态是不透明的信息。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“很多时候人们做事情是因为他们内心有感受，如果我们对此好奇，可以帮助我们更好地理解他人”等陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Here are a few examples of psychoeducational statements which could be used in response to material from the session: “You know, many times when people do what they do, it is because they have feelings inside them and if we are curious about that, it can help us to try and make more sense of other people”.
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了心理教育陈述的示例。

atoms.claim: 当出现非心智化时，可以通过指出假设和过度思考来应对。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“听起来你对X的感受做了假设。当我们对别人的感受做假设时，很容易出错”等陈述。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: We could also address non-mentalizing when it occurs, by saying something like: “It sounds as if you have made an assumption about what X was feeling. You know when we make assumptions about what people feel, we can easily get it wrong - ….”
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了应对非心智化的具体陈述。

atoms.claim: 当过度思考时，可以暂停并提醒自己无法真正看透他人的想法。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“我们可以暂停一下吗？我想知道你是否开始过度思考了。当我们过度思考时，会对别人的想法做出大量假设，并把这些假设当作事实。”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “Can we pause for a minute, I was wondering if you are beginning to overthink a bit, and you know when we overthink, we start making massive assumptions about other people’s minds and then we start to treat these assumptions as if they are facts, when they aren’t– we cannot really see into other people’s minds.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了应对过度思考的陈述。

atoms.claim: 焦虑时，头脑可能会失控并做出假设，最好的做法是停下来，询问对方的感受。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“当我们焦虑时，头脑有时会失控，对别人的想法或感受做出假设。最好的做法是停下来，问问对方在想什么或感受什么。”
atoms.evidence_excerpt: “When we are anxious our minds can sometimes run away with us and make assumptions of what other people are thinking or feeling, but the best thing to do when we catch ourselves making assumptions or overthinking, is to stop, pause and perhaps ask the other person what they are thinking or feeling.”
atoms.extraction_notes: 直接引用了焦虑时的应对陈述。

atoms.claim: 心理教育工作坊可以全天进行，或分几次进行，通常以小组形式由两名临床医生主持。
therapeutic_implications: 工作坊包括破冰练习、关于青少年大脑的简短教学、电影片段讨论、关系理解、自我伤害理解、暴力理解等环节。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Psychoeducational workshops can be conducted over the course of a whole day or over a couple of sessions. They are usually offered in a group format and best delivered by two clinicians.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了工作坊的时长、形式和人员配置。

atoms.claim: 在理解自我伤害的环节中，使用卡片上的陈述让参与者判断对错，并讨论如何帮助自伤者。
therapeutic_implications: 使用如“自伤是为了引起注意”或“我的孩子自伤时就是有自杀倾向”等陈述，通过讨论来澄清误解。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Understanding self-harm: In our service, instead of giving didactic input on self-harm, we wrote several statements on cards which were handed out to everyone. Participants took turns to read the statements on the card and then they had to say whether they thought the statement was true or false.
atoms.extraction_notes: 描述了自我伤害环节的具体方法。

validation_errors.error: evidence_excerpt is not verbatim in source chunk

atom.claim: 在理解和管理暴力环节中，使用卡片排序活动，让参与者按最有益的顺序排列行动，包括给予空间、冷静、讨论事件和修复。
therapeutic_implications: 卡片上的行动包括“给予空间”、“冷静下来”、“讨论事件并承认自己的贡献”以及“修复”。
atom.evidence_excerpt: Understanding and managing violence: ... the group is handed a group of cards with actions written on it and they are tasked to arrange the cards in the most helpful order of what needs to happen next. Each card contains an action in a mentalizing sequence, going from “giving space” to “calm down” to finally discussing the event and owning up to their own contributions to the event. The last card is for reparation.
atom.extraction_notes: 描述了暴力管理环节的具体活动。

atoms.canonical_name_zh: 非心理化互动处理流程
atoms.claim: 处理非心理化互动的流程是：停止并暂停，表达共情并验证感受，倒回到失去心理化能力的时刻，询问细节，使用验证、共情、阐述和探索来开启心理化，温和地处理非心理化错误。
therapeutic_implications: 倒回到心理化能力丧失的时刻
心理化当时无法被心理化的感受
response_constraints: 温和地处理非心理化错误
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Non-mentalizing action – STOP and PAUSE – expressing empathy and trying to validate what the young person felt at the time, even if this is based on them not mentalizing – then trying to rewind to the moment where the young person lost the ability to mentalize – then asking for detail and using validation, empathy as well as elaboration and exploration to open things up and in the process trying to kick start mentalizing by gently addressing the non-mentalizing errors which may have escalated the emotions or driven the person into impulsive action.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述了非心理化互动的处理步骤。

atoms.claim: 治疗师应保持好奇、温暖和不知情的姿态，并积极工作。
therapeutic_implications: 使用支持和共情作为主要技术
在支持共情与情感阐述或挑战之间移动
atoms.evidence_excerpt: we are active in work and convey a stance of curiosity, warmth and not-knowing. Support and empathy are the techniques used most of the time and we move between support and empathy and affect elaboration or challenging most of the time in our attempt to foster basic mentalizing.

atom.evidence_excerpt: To promote mentalizing of the mind/body links within the whole family, we have sometimes invited the adolescent’s parents to bring in photos of themselves when they were the age of their child. Parents were asked to examine their photos and to share what was seen and unseen, while their children were encouraged to be curious and ask questions. The parents were instructed not to answer as adults, but as their adolescent self might have answered. This helped parents connect with their own adolescent experiences, and many would share stories of shame and awkwardness, as well as challenges with their changing bodies. This exercise brought humour into the therapeutic room, and adolescents would often be really interested and surprised that their parents had had similar experiences. Emotional stories were elicited, many of which parents had never shared before with their child. ... The photograph exercise helped create a transitional space, where adolescents could trust their parents as people who could possibly understand the challenges they were facing.

atom.evidence_excerpt: It feels encouraging to see gender diverse young people demonstrate stronger mentalizing capacities over time. This usually involves a willingness and a capacity to put themselves in other people’s shoes (e.g. “my mum has known me as “Katie” for 14 years, I get it why she slips sometimes and that it isn’t intentional”), a capacity to tolerate difference in thinking (“I understand why people were a bit confused when I came out as Georgia at school, as I’d always tried to appear very masculine”), the courage to express uncertainty (“I’m not sure why I’ve been feeling this way or what it means exactly”), and difference within the peer group (“my Trans friends think that cisgender people don’t understand, but I have felt at times understood, and at other times misunderstood by people and this doesn’t always have to do with whether you’re Trans”), an ability to imagine that mental states such as feelings about the body may be different over time (“I know I’d like to have surgery in the future, but I also know what I want might change and that’d be OK, too”), and a capacity to engage with exploration in a curious, open, and non-defensive way. As noted elsewhere (Bateman & Fonagy, 2006), highlighting and reinforcing positive mentalizing is just as important as noticing mentalizing struggles.
atom.extraction_notes: 明确描述了性别多元青少年心智化能力的具体表现。

atom.evidence_excerpt: when I speak about at-risk mental states (ARMS), I am referring to the term used by mental health professionals to describe young people who are experiencing early, low-level signs of psychosis. The National Health Service in the UK describes three groups of young people who may be said to present ARMS. First, those who have been functioning less well over the last 12 months. This would include individuals who have withdrawn from school, college or work or have not been able to spend time with family or friends. Second, people with short-lived or milder symptoms of psychosis within the last three months, and third, persons who experience brief or limited intermittent psychotic symptoms. These are psychotic-level symptoms that have naturally ceased within seven days.

atoms.claim: 认识论信任是通过青少年体验到被看见、被理解（即被准确心智化）而赢得的。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Research into Epistemic Trust suggests that this is ‘won’ when the young person experiences themselves as being seen (re-cognised) and understood; mentalized accurately, as it were.

atoms.claim: 一般精神病理学因子（P因子）可能是个体认识论信任适应性差的代理指标。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Ideas about the General Psychopathology Factor (“P-Factor”, Caspi et al., 2014) have led to the proposal that this transdiagnostic approach to the risk of chronicity and treatment resistance in an individual may in fact be a proxy measure for this disposition; one of poor or low adaptability of a person’s Epistemic Trust.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文提出P因子可能是认识论信任适应性差的代理指标，属于强烈暗示。

atoms.claim: 那些常被服务描述为“难以接触”的青少年，实际上可能更应被描述为“服务不足”：他们得到的帮助（通常是大剂量、复杂且昂贵的）很少被体验为有帮助，他们的拒绝在某种意义上是有目的且适应性的。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The vignette above is a typical example of the ‘dis-integration’ of the care system around those challenging young people, who are frequently described as “hard to reach” by services, although in truth they might better be described as “under-served”: the help that is offered to them (often in large, complex, and expensive ‘doses’) is rarely experienced as helpful, and their rejection of it is, in that sense at least, purposeful and adaptive.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将“难以接触”重新定义为“服务不足”，并指出拒绝帮助是有目的且适应性的。

atoms.claim: 对于认识论过度警觉的青少年，帮助之门对专业帮助者紧闭，却对毒品贩子、帮派头目等黑暗社会代表敞开，这些黑暗角色似乎更容易被他们不加批判地理解和接受。
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Paradoxically, while the doors to help seem firmly closed to professional helpers, they can appear frustratingly (or worryingly) open to the representatives of the darker side of society: drug dealers, gang leaders, delinquent peers and adults who might want to exploit them. Something about these darker characters (who the young person may, in truth, identify as their existing network of ‘help’) seems much easier for them to understand and accept uncritically.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了这一悖论。

atom.claim: 严重精神、社会、教育等复杂交叉问题（包括多重不良经历）的青少年可能发展出“认识论过度警觉”，即对工作者或帮助者所提供的学习、经验、知识或建议的社会价值持持续且普遍的怀疑倾向。
atom.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT has been developed for young people whose severe psychiatric, social, educational, and other complex intersecting problems, including multiple adverse experiences, have called forth adaptive responses that have been labelled as “epistemic hypervigilance”; a sustained and pervasive tendency towards mistrust in the social value of any of the learning, experience, knowledge or advice that workers or helpers may hold and offer to them by way of help.
atom.extraction_notes: 原文明确描述了认识论过度警觉的定义及其与复杂问题的关联。

clinical_signals: 倾向于信任剥削性人物
therapeutic_implications: 治疗需解决青少年对帮助本身的关系问题
atom.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT has been developed for young people whose severe psychiatric, social, educational, and other complex intersecting problems, including multiple adverse experiences, have called forth adaptive responses that have been labelled as “epistemic hypervigilance”; a sustained and pervasive tendency towards mistrust in the social value of any of the learning, experience, knowledge or advice that workers or helpers may hold and offer to them by way of help.
atom.extraction_notes: 直接定义认知过度警觉。

atom.claim: 高P因子可能反映个体认知信任的可塑性低，导致循证治疗对其效果不佳。
therapeutic_implications: 对于高P因子个体，治疗需先建立认知信任
atom.evidence_excerpt: Ideas about the General Psychopathology Factor (“P-Factor”, Caspi et al., 2014) have led to the proposal that this transdiagnostic approach to the risk of chronicity and treatment resistance in an individual may in fact be a proxy measure for this disposition; one of poor or low adaptability of a person’s Epistemic Trust. Evidence-based treatments may work well (however severe the symptoms) for individuals with a low P-factor but appear to “bounce off” those with high P-factors because of their fundamental inability to trust the value of the help on offer
atom.extraction_notes: 文本提出高P因子与认知信任可塑性低相关，并暗示治疗可能无效。

atoms.claim: AMBIT影响下的服务可能将其更基本的任务视为能够解决来访者的慢性认识论警觉——解决来访者与帮助本身的关系。
therapeutic_implications: 服务需关注来访者与帮助的关系
建立认识论信任
atoms.evidence_excerpt: an AMBIT-influenced service may see its more fundamental task as being able to address this chronic Epistemic Hypervigilance in their clients – to address their clients’ relationship to help itself.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述AMBIT服务的基本任务

atoms.claim: 认识论信任不尊重专业角色、权威或培训——年轻人可能更容易与低薪、系统上被忽视的寄宿护理人员建立认识论信任，而不是与昂贵的、高资质的治疗师。
clinical_signals: 与某些工作者建立信任困难
therapeutic_implications: 重视非专业关系中的信任建立
降低对专业角色的依赖
atoms.evidence_excerpt: Epistemic Trust shows no respect for a professional role, authority, or training – a young person may find it much easier to develop some epistemic trust in a low paid, systemically-overlooked residential care worker than in an expensive, highly qualified therapist with multiple degrees and diplomas!
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述认识论信任的特点

atoms.claim: 在压力下，工作者变得目的论化，权力斗争常常被暗中或有时公开地演绎。
therapeutic_implications: 支持工作者保持心智化
减少跨机构冲突
atoms.evidence_excerpt: They become teleological, and power struggles are often enacted, covertly or sometimes overtly.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述工作者在压力下进入目的论模式

atoms.claim: AMBIT是一套系统应用的原则和方法，旨在帮助工作人员更容易识别服务系统何时解体（停止相互心智化），并拥有干预工具以恢复心智化。
therapeutic_implications: 使用AMBIT工具恢复心智化
系统层面的干预
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT can best be described as a set of principles and methods applied systemically that stimulate awareness of the above problems and help staff working with these kinds of clients to recognise more easily when and where the service systems dis-integrate (stop mentalizing each other), and then have tools to intervene to restore mentalizing.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确描述AMBIT的定义和功能

atoms.claim: 大多数这些年轻人有依恋系统受损的历史；他们很少拥有安全依恋模型来支持与专业人员建立帮助性治疗关系。
therapeutic_implications: 需要特别关注依恋问题
建立信任需耐心
atoms.evidence_excerpt: most of these young people have a history in which their attachment systems have been compromised; they rarely have a model of secure attachment that they can use to support the task of building a helping therapeutic relationship with a professional.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述青少年依恋系统受损

atoms.claim: 如果儿童的依恋系统是紊乱的，心智化能力的发展尤其受到抑制。
therapeutic_implications: 早期干预依恋问题
促进心智化发展
atoms.evidence_excerpt: The development of mentalizing capacity (see Chapter 1) is inhibited particularly if a child’s attachment system is disorganised (Fonagy & Target, 2005).
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述依恋紊乱对心智化发展的影响

atoms.claim: 我们在不可避免的压力条件下工作，尽管我们尽力心智化，但这种能力变得脆弱。
therapeutic_implications: 支持工作者应对压力
提供心智化支持
atoms.evidence_excerpt: we work in conditions where stress is inevitable, and where despite our best efforts to mentalize, this capacity is rendered fragile.
atoms.extraction_notes: 明确陈述工作者心智化能力的脆弱性

therapeutic_implications: 关注社会网络对心智化的支持
促进社会联系

atoms.evidence_excerpt: mentalizing capacity as a measure of a person’s social connectedness (at least as much as it is an individual or dyadic phenomenon).

atoms.evidence_excerpt: The mother can only mentalize her screaming infant insofar as she has at least the idea of a network of other minds that can, would, or do hold her own mind in mind: her own mother, her partner, her friend, the health visitor, etc.

atoms.claim: 潜在脆弱性随着社会稀疏化而直接增加，个体发现越来越难以接触到良性的、具有心智化的心智。
therapeutic_implications: 干预应致力于防止或逆转社会稀疏化
atoms.evidence_excerpt: a latent vulnerability that increases in direct relation to “social thinning” (McCrory, 2019), so that across time an individual, through neurodevelopmental vulnerability, trauma, or symptomatic illness, finds they have less and less access to benign and mentalizing minds.

atoms.claim: AMBIT是一种团队方法，尽管它强调可能产生认识信任的强个体关键关系。
therapeutic_implications: 干预应基于团队，同时培养关键个体关系
atoms.evidence_excerpt: AMBIT is a team approach, even though it emphasises strong individual “key” relationships where epistemic trust may arise.
atoms.extraction_notes: 原文明确将AMBIT描述为团队方法。

atoms.canonical_name_en: epistemic trust independent of professional role

therapeutic_implications: 不应假设高资质自动带来认识信任
